answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to anchor its work to a shared public reef: a ledger of verifiable tasks completed over time. New accounts start with no history, so a flood of fresh identities cannot fake the depth of a long-lived participant. Old contributions act like a relic, proof of sustained effort that cannot be minted overnight. Reputation then grows only along a visible horizon of real work, and peers stake their own standing when they vouch, so creating a thousand sock puppets buys no trust, only empty shells.
